ai.text:
This proposal would change the EU's rules for tracking and checking emissions from ships. Right now, two separate systems cover this: one for greenhouse gas emissions under the EU Emissions Trading System, and one for the energy ships use, under the FuelEU Maritime rules. Because the two systems are similar but formally separate, shipping companies have to repeat many compliance steps and deal with the same authorities twice.

The aim is to merge them into a single system. The existing monitoring, reporting and verification rules would be widened to cover energy use as well as emissions and energy efficiency data. Companies would include all the required information in one monitoring plan and one emissions report, submitted through a common process. The checking rules would be updated to match, and the Commission would be given power to adjust the detailed methods later so they work for the broader scope. The proposal also brings some definitions and reporting requirements closer to those used by the International Maritime Organization's data collection system, and it clarifies which authority is responsible for these duties.

The proposal also makes some targeted changes. It would extend the EU Emissions Trading System to certain categories of ships, to create a more even playing field, with the Commission given powers to set the related monitoring and reporting rules. It adds specific safeguards against vessels engaged in or supporting offshore operations avoiding their obligations. The proposal is a regulation of the European Parliament and the Council, which decide on it together under the ordinary legislative procedure, on an equal footing.
